payload.description: Umbrella for closing the gap that a leaked cluster-stored deployer key can stand up operational routes and (today) drain existing routes. Sub-issues cover: moving ISM + warp-route ownership to the hardware wallet, gating the relayer with a curated route whitelist, and minimizing the deploy-time signer. See docs/architecture-decisions.md (deployer authorization) and docs/ops-decisions.md.
payload.title: Harden warp-route deploy authorization & deployer-key custody (SVM bridge)

payload.description:
The core deployer SKIPS the multisig-ISM ownership transfer on a stale assumption. deployer-scripts-config/deploy.sh:298-306 says "core transfer-ownership does not exist in the CLI ... Skipping", but `hyperlane-sealevel-client multisig-ism-message-id transfer-ownership --program-id <ism> <new-owner>` DOES exist (verified at the pinned monorepo sha 16c056a, client main.rs:676).

Impact: the ISM access-control owner = deployer key today. multisig-ism-message-id `SetValidatorsAndThreshold` enforces only owner-signer (processor.rs:374-376), so a leaked key can swap in attacker validators and forge messages for EVERY route on that ISM -> drain all collateral. This is the most severe residual hole.

Fix: replace the multisig_ism_message_id "Skipping" branch with a real transfer-ownership to HARDWARE_WALLET_PUBKEY, mirroring the working mailbox transfer-ownership block (deploy.sh:289-295). validator_announce has no owner / nothing owner-gated (instruction.rs = Init,Announce only) -> drop its warning, nothing to transfer. No monorepo bump needed (command present at the pin).
payload.title: Transfer multisig-ISM ownership to the hardware wallet during core deploy

payload.description:
warp-deployer-scripts-config/deploy.sh transfers only the route programs BPF upgrade authority (solana program set-upgrade-authority, deploy.sh:254-259). The Hyperlane app-level owner is never moved, and build_side (deploy.sh:62-75) sets no owner -> defaults to the deployer key.

Impact: that owner gates enroll_remote_routers / set_interchain_security_module / set_destination_gas / transfer_ownership on each route. A leaked key can re-point a routers or change an existing route ISM and drain that route collateral.

Fix: after deploy + the upgrade-authority transfer, call `hyperlane-sealevel-client token transfer-ownership` (exists at pin, main.rs:346; --token-type Native|Synthetic|Collateral per side, --program-id) to move each side owner to HARDWARE_WALLET_PUBKEY. Run LAST, after all owner-gated config (enroll/set-ISM/set-dest-gas) the client does during deploy. Note: once transferred, FORCE_REDEPLOY of an EXISTING route requires the hardware wallet (Ledger) to sign owner ops - acceptable/expected.
payload.title: Transfer warp-route app-level ownership to the hardware wallet during warp deploy

payload.description:
Relayer relays EVERY message between gorchain<->solana: no whitelist set, and HYP_GASPAYMENTENFORCEMENT=[{"type":"none"}] (docker-compose-hyperlane-relayer.yml). Empty MatchingList = relay-all (relayer matching_list.rs:369-375). The mailbox is permissionless (processor.rs dispatch/process), so any deployed route is operational with ZERO operator action; the warp-UI listing is cosmetic.

HYP_WHITELIST is a built-in relayer MatchingList setting (relayer settings mod.rs:50, loaded via the HYP_ env prefix, hyperlane-base loader mod.rs:98) -> config only, no agent code.

Fix: populate HYP_WHITELIST with blessed routes recipient addresses (recipientaddress = H256 hex from each route program-ids.json), assembled in the ops layer from the CURATED git route menu (mirror the warpRoutes.yaml build path), regenerated + relayer restarted when a route is added.

CRITICAL: derive from the curated git source, NOT on-chain discovery - else a leaked-key rogue route auto-whitelists itself and the gate is void. Updating the whitelist is an ops/git-reviewed config change (NOT Ledger): that is the route-endorsement governance gate.
payload.title: Gate the relayer with HYP_WHITELIST built from the curated route menu

payload.description: publish-bridge-state.yml regex-patches deployment-derived scalars (IGP IDs, mailbox, and now HYP_WHITELIST per hyp-d9c.3) into committed specs (spec-relayer.yml/spec-gas-oracle.yml/spec-warp-ui.yml) then commits+pushes. Preferred: derive these on-the-fly from the deployer's generated/ artifacts at deploy time instead of mutating committed specs. Separate concern from hyp-d9c; raised during the authz-hardening design 2026-06-09.
payload.title: Derive prod consumer config from generated artifacts (drop committed-spec patching)

payload.description:
The ops layer (PRs #25/#30) implemented bring-up (deploy-all.yml, setup-all.yml, prepare-chains, distribute-credentials, configure-dns, publish-bridge-state, stop-all) but NONE of the operator-attended maintenance playbooks the design calls for. docs/ops-decisions.md:54-62 specifies seven composite playbooks; ops/playbooks/ contains none of them:

  kill-switch.yml      MISSING
  restore.yml          MISSING
  ism-update.yml       MISSING
  teardown.yml         MISSING
  add-validator.yml    MISSING
  remove-validator.yml MISSING
  verify-ownership.yml MISSING

Trigger: ops can now deploy N validators off validators.yaml (deploy-all.yml Validators play, ~lines 132-186) — pod + MinIO IAM + DNS — but nothing updates the on-chain multisig ISM validator set. A newly-deployed validator announces to validator-announce and writes checkpoints to MinIO, but its H160 is not in any ISM, so the relayer's ISM verification ignores its signatures. The deployment side and the on-chain side were designed as separate operator actions (docs/architecture-decisions.md:310-312); only the deployment side shipped.

All on-chain steps sign via the forked hyperlane-sealevel-client with BUILT-IN LEDGER support (--keypair usb://ledger...), run on the operator's localhost, sign+broadcast in one step (docs/ops-decisions.md:7-45). 

BLOCKED ON: validation of the Ledger-support PRs (forked sealevel-client + hyperlane fork) currently under test. Implementation should not start until that signing path is confirmed working.

Reference: the archived single-validator k8s-Job pattern in deployment/ops-archive/scripts/restore.sh + templates/restore-job.yml.j2 shows the old set-validators-and-threshold call shape (pre-Ledger, pre-ansible). Authoritative spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-29-ops-layer-redesign-and-ledger-signing-design.md. Builds on the ISM-ownership-handoff work in hyp-d9c (Ledger owns the ISM, so it can authorize set-validators-and-threshold).
payload.title: Implement operator-attended bridge maintenance ops playbooks (Ledger-signed)

payload.description: see above
payload.title: ism-update.yml — set ISM (validators, threshold) per chain, Ledger-signed

payload.description: Structural gap behind hyp-81f: the deployer Job can only ever set ONE validator per chain on-chain. deployer-multisig-config/{gorchain,solana}-multisig.json.tmpl hardcode a single ${X_VALIDATOR_ADDRESS} scalar with threshold 1; the scalars come from group_vars/all.yml (ops/inventories/prod/group_vars/all.yml:58-59) and are rendered once by deploy.sh:190-218. There is no path for a multi-validator initial deployment. Decide whether the deployer should derive its multisig config from validators.yaml (same H160-resolution logic ism-update needs) so a fresh deploy and a later ism-update agree on the data source, or whether initial deploy stays single-validator and ism-update is the only multi-validator path. Coupled to hyp-81f's data-model decision.
payload.title: Make initial ISM config multi-validator (derive from validators.yaml)

payload.description: ops/playbooks/kill-switch.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:56). Emergency halt: 'deployment stop' the agents, then set ISM validators to the null set per chain via the Ledger client (set-validators-and-threshold with the 0x0..0 sentinel, see deployment/ops-archive/scripts/*.sh for the old shape). Pairs with restore.yml. Reuses the ism-update set-validators primitive. Blocked on Ledger-client validation.
payload.title: kill-switch.yml — stop agents + null the ISM validator set per chain

payload.description: ops/playbooks/restore.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:57). Inverse of kill-switch: set ISM validators back to the real set per chain (derived from validators.yaml) via the Ledger client, then 'deployment start' the agents. Reuses the ism-update primitive. Blocked on Ledger-client validation.
payload.title: restore.yml — restore real ISM validator set + start agents

payload.description: ops/playbooks/add-validator.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:60). Interactive: generate spec-validator-<label>.yml + edit validators.yaml, human gate (commit/PR/merge), then distribute-credentials -> configure-dns -> minio resync -> deploy the validator via stack_deploy. On-chain ISM addition is a SEPARATE ism-update.yml run (hyp-81f) — this playbook only stands up the pod/MinIO-IAM/DNS. Mirrors the existing deploy-all.yml Validators play (lines ~132-186) but for a single new validator.
payload.title: add-validator.yml — deployment-side validator onboarding

payload.description: ops/playbooks/remove-validator.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:61). Pre-flight: ism-update.yml (hyp-81f) must have detached the validator from the ISM first. Then: 'deployment stop' the validator -> interactive spec deletion + validators.yaml edit + commit gate -> MinIO IAM cleanup (delete the per-validator user, keep its bucket) -> remove DNS. Per-validator MinIO IAM model is in ops/roles/credentials (PR #18, 93bfba3).
payload.title: remove-validator.yml — deployment-side validator offboarding

payload.description: ops/playbooks/teardown.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:59). Operator-attended multi-step flow: 'deployment stop' agents -> loop {claim IGP fees per chain} -> loop {close program} -> close orphan buffers -> loop {transfer SOL per wallet} -> optional key disposal. Each on-chain step signs on the Ledger. Sequencing/pauses/retry belong in the playbook, not a shell script. Blocked on Ledger-client validation.
payload.title: teardown.yml — attended bridge teardown (fees, programs, SOL, keys)

payload.description: ops/playbooks/verify-ownership.yml (docs/ops-decisions.md:62). Read-only, no signing: confirm every deployed program (mailbox, ISM, IGP, validator-announce, warp routes) is owned by the hardware-wallet address. Companion to the hyp-d9c ownership handoff. Note: hyp-405 (Extend verify-ownership to check app-level ISM/route owners) is the follow-up that broadens this once the base playbook exists — base implementation belongs here.
payload.title: verify-ownership.yml — read-only program-ownership audit

payload.body: Resolved by #34 (a7ad1a5): deployment-derived values (mailbox, IGP program-ids/accounts, relayer whitelist) now render at deploy time from generated/ via ops/roles/stack_deploy/tasks/render_spec.yml — committed specs hold placeholder tokens (__GORCHAIN_MAILBOX__, __*_IGP_*__, __RELAYER_WHITELIST__) substituted into the on-host spec, gated by spec_render_generated. publish-bridge-state.yml no longer patches specs; it commits only generated/.

DEFERRED (2026-06-10): maintenance ops (this epic, incl. ism-update 564.1 and add/remove-validator 564.5/.6) deferred. Priority order: (1) WebSocket-based indexing (must land before deployment — it changes how the bridge indexes chains), (2) bridge deployment, (3) this epic. ism-update design is captured at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-ism-update-playbook-design.md (design-only, no code). Resume at the writing-plans step.

payload.description: Replace poll-based event detection with WebSocket subscriptions, make Solana/gorchain commitment configurable, and remove every multi-second sleep from the message critical path. Target ~2.5-4s gorchain / ~3-5s solana delivery in fast (confirmed) mode. Must land BEFORE bridge deployment (changes how the bridge indexes chains). Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-websocket-fast-bridging-design.md (supersedes the 2026-05-25 tentative spec; adversarially reviewed 2026-06-10 — old spec covered only 1 of 3 polling stages, omitted gorchain, and routed a secret into committed state).

payload.description: New chains/hyperlane-sealevel/src/pubsub.rs (~100-150 lines) on solana_pubsub_client (workspace dep solana-pubsub-client=3.0, unused today): subscribe at the SAME commitment as indexing_commitment, notify_waiters on event, 60s pings (Helius 10min idle drop), reconnect w/ backoff, silent fallback to timer. ConnectionConf gains ws_url; config via wsUrls/customWsUrls mirroring rpcUrls/customRpcUrls (parser/mod.rs:189) so HYP_CHAINS_<CHAIN>_CUSTOMWSURLS works. Expose via NEW Indexer<T> trait method wake_signal() default None (avoids ContractSync::new signature change + downcasting); ContractSync select!{sleep, notified} at mod.rs:265-273. CRITICAL (missed by old spec): validator has TWO loops — SealevelMerkleTreeHookIndexer (accountSubscribe on merkle tree account; covered by shared ContractSync change) and checkpoint_submitter (submit.rs:121-166, NOT a ContractSync — pass Notify in, select! at sleeps lines 152+165). Validator must be event-driven or relayer loses the checkpoint race into 5s/10s/30s backoff (pending_message.rs:922). Spec §4.2/§2.
payload.title: Fork: WebSocket wake-up for relayer AND validator (pubsub.rs + Indexer::wake_signal)

payload.description: Add indexing_commitment to ConnectionConf (trait_builder.rs:15-30), thread through hardcoded finalized reads: account.rs:39 (3 callers: mailbox_indexer.rs:82,179 + interchain_gas.rs:139), mailbox_indexer.rs:101,201, interchain_gas.rs:159, merkle_tree_hook.rs:68 (+relax assertion msgs :22,:36), rpc/client.rs:136,165,222,251. LEAVE finalized: provider.rs:176-180 blockhash fetch. Chain-level commitment key, env HYP_CHAINS_<CHAIN>_COMMITMENT. Security: the risky hop is the VALIDATOR signing over a confirmed slot — destination mint can't be clawed back on origin rollback; no safe hybrid (validator gates delivery). Default finalized; fast mode explicit opt-in. WS subscription commitment MUST match (else wasted wake-ups). Spec §4.1/D5.
payload.title: Fork: configurable commitment level (finalized default, confirmed opt-in)

payload.description: New env vars (chain-specific canonical pattern): SOLANA_WS_URL (SECRET — Helius key; spec secrets: like SOLANA_RPC_URL), GORCHAIN_WS_URL, SOLANA_COMMITMENT/GORCHAIN_COMMITMENT. Delivery env-only via HYP_CHAINS_*_CUSTOMRPCURLS/CUSTOMWSURLS/COMMITMENT in relayer+validator compose — agent-config.json/registry carry placeholders only (depends on hyp-f9d). Keep-in-sync ripple: compose -> deployment/spec-*.yml -> tests/e2e/fixtures/test-spec-*.yml -> stack_env_vars in ops/inventories/*/group_vars/all.yml. Gorchain WS reachability: pubsub on RPC port+1 (8900); e2e external-services ip: entries gain WS port (gorchain-rpc:8900, solana :18900); prod/staging expose 8900 + verify proxy passes wss upgrade. e2e: (1) WS happy path w/ subscription-establishment log assert, (2) kill-WS fallback to timer polling, (3) confirmed-mode smoke beating finalized baseline, (4) secret-free state asserts, (5) warp-ui mode-flag fixture check. Spec §5/§8.
payload.title: Stacks: WS/commitment env plumbing, gorchain WS port, e2e tests

payload.description: hyperlane-warp-ui-template fork. Fast mode inverts ordering: delivery (~3-5s) precedes origin finality (~13-15s); the gap IS the rollback window. Transfer view shows two independent signals: Delivered (existing delivery tracking) and Final (origin tx reached finalized — getSignatureStatuses upgrade-only check). Fast: Sent -> Delivered ('awaiting origin finality') -> Complete; never claim irreversibility before origin finality. Safe-mode collapse via runtime-injected flag (pod env at container start, like runtime route config — NOT build-time NEXT_PUBLIC inline), derived from the same SOLANA_COMMITMENT spec var the agents use, so UI and agents can't disagree; safe mode suppresses the finality badge (single-stage Sent -> Complete). Spec §7/D7.
payload.title: Warp-UI: dual-commitment UX (Delivered vs Final, safe-mode collapse)

payload.description: Rebase gorbagana branch (2 commits: 82ab03c064 CI removal, a2f6ef11b0 Ledger signing) onto upstream 4da9c4419a (agents v2.2.0 release). Upstream didn't touch rust/sealevel/client in range — Ledger commit rebases clean. Contract sources are semantically unchanged in range (only a variable-name typo fix in mailbox/src/processor.rs + build-script churn; verified 2026-06-10). Convert kms-endpoint.patch + s3-path-style.patch (container-build/gorbagana-dev-hyperlane-agent/) into commits, checking v2.2.0 didn't obsolete them (s3_storage.rs/signers.rs saw only chore+tron churn); drop patch steps from the Dockerfile. Retag (sealevel-vX.Y.Z-gorbagana.N), rebuild agent+deployer images. Nothing is deployed yet (staging included) — the new base is the first provenance pin for every environment. Spec §4.0/D1/D2.

wss://rpc.gorbagana.wtf/ upgrade handshake returns 502 (backpack.gorbagana.wtf too) while HTTP RPC on the same host is healthy (getHealth ok) — verified 2026-06-10. Node side is fine: agave runs --full-rpc-api with pubsub on 8900 bound 0.0.0.0; gorbagana-rpc compose exposes 8900; envoy-rpc.yaml routes Upgrade: websocket to agave_ws:8900. Root cause: gorbagana-rpc deployment/spec.yml declares websocket: true routes but SO's http-proxy has NO websocket support — key silently ignored (verified: zero handling in stack-orchestrator/stack_orchestrator/deploy/). Workaround patch-caddy-websocket.sh (gorbagana-rpc stacks/gorchain-rpc/deploy/) PUTs an in-memory route via Caddy admin API: lost on Caddy restart, dials a {deployment-id}-service FQDN that goes stale on redeploy, and forces ingress protocols to [h1] globally. Fix: native websocket: true support in SO ingress generation (deploy/k8s/cluster_info.py — SO is under our control), delete the patch script. Fallback: expose 8900 directly on the gorchain host. Gates prod/staging WS rollout for the bridge agents (they need gorchain WS whenever off the RPC host).
payload.title: Gorchain public WS endpoint broken (502) — SO http-proxy ignores websocket: true

payload.body: Design validated 2026-06-10: SO-only fix (no controller access needed) — SO generates a per-deployment ws-mux (caddy:2-alpine ConfigMap+Deployment+Service) doing the Upgrade split; Ingress gets a single backend per (host,path), fixing the duplicate-paths bug too. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-so-websocket-ingress-design.md. First implementation step is the §6 spike (101 handshake through controller→mux without the h1 forcing).

payload.description: Minor findings from final review of the SO websocket-mux implementation (stack-orchestrator branch websocket-mux), none blocking: (1) _path_matcher glob /sub* also matches /subother — diverges from Ingress Prefix segment semantics; fix with 'path /sub /sub/*' (ws_mux.py:_path_matcher). (2) host/path interpolated raw into the Caddyfile — operator-authored so not a security boundary, but reject whitespace/braces/quotes in validate_http_proxy_routes as defense-in-depth. (3) collect_mux_entries splits proxy-to with bare unpack — malformed extra-colon value raises ugly ValueError at up; align with plain-route tolerance or validate format at create. (4) removing all websocket routes from a spec leaves the old mux Deployment/Service/CM orphaned until down (harmless; Ingress no longer references it) — consider deleting mux objects at up when get_ws_mux_resources() is None. Context: hyp-d34.7, spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-so-websocket-ingress-design.md.
payload.title: ws-mux follow-ups: path matcher semantics, input hardening, stale-mux GC

payload.body: SO implementation complete on stack-orchestrator branch websocket-mux (11 commits, 39 unit tests). Kind verification passed end-to-end: create-time validation rejects duplicate routes; single-backend ingress; 101 handshake + echo round-trip through controller→mux with NO h1 forcing (spec §6 risk did not materialize); controller-restart and stop/start-redeploy regressions green; down sweeps mux. Two extra fixes from final review: case-insensitive Upgrade matcher (header_regexp, lowercase clients verified 101) and Caddyfile-hash pod annotation (config changes roll the mux). Bonus fix: disable-ssl-redirect annotation on no-TLS (kind) ingresses — previously ALL kind HTTP routes 308d into cert-less HTTPS. Remaining: Task 9 rollout (SO merge + host upgrade + gorbagana-rpc patch-script removal + live wss check).

TLS round verified locally (2026-06-10, kind + self-signed SAN cert via Ingress spec.tls): HTTPS GET through controller→mux returns 200 over negotiated HTTP/2; wss handshake (ALPN http/1.1, the real WS-client path) → 101; encrypted websocat echo round-trip OK. ALPN concern closed — no protocol forcing needed. OPERATIONAL NOTE for rollout: fork controller has a cert-load ordering quirk — it pushes Caddy config BEFORE writing Ingress-TLS secret pems to /etc/caddy/certs (load_folders), and skips re-push when regenerated config is identical, so a newly-loaded cert isn't served until the next MATERIAL config push. Symptom: 'tlsv1 alert internal error' on a host whose secret exists. Workaround: apply+delete a dummy ingress (or any real ingress change) to force a push. Could explain transient TLS failures after fresh deploys on prod; ACME-issued certs go through caddy storage, not load_folders, so steady-state prod is unaffected.

RESOLVED — verified live on woodburn 2026-06-10 after SO upgrade + RPC redeploy: wss://rpc.gorbagana.wtf and wss://backpack.gorbagana.wtf handshake 101 (was 502); slotSubscribe returns subscription id and streams slotNotifications through LE TLS -> caddy ingress -> ws-mux -> agave:8900; getHealth ok on both hosts; http->https 308 redirect preserved (acme-email gate); agave pod untouched by the rollout (22d uptime, 0 restarts). patch-caddy-websocket.sh removed in gorbagana-rpc (branch drop-caddy-ws-patch, pending user push). Gorchain WS endpoint dependency for the fast-bridging epic (hyp-d34) is now UNBLOCKED.

payload.description: Rebase gorbagana branch (2 commits: 82ab03c064 CI removal, a2f6ef11b0 Ledger signing) onto upstream 4da9c4419a (agents v2.2.0 release). Upstream didn't touch rust/sealevel/client in range — Ledger commit rebases clean. Contract sources are semantically unchanged in range (only a variable-name typo fix in mailbox/src/processor.rs + build-script churn; verified 2026-06-10). Convert kms-endpoint.patch + s3-path-style.patch (container-build/gorbagana-dev-hyperlane-agent/) into commits, checking v2.2.0 didn't obsolete them (s3_storage.rs/signers.rs saw only chore+tron churn); drop patch steps from the Dockerfile. Delivery per fork PR flow: branch gorbagana-v2.2.0 (base+reviewed lineage) repoints the default branch; the 2 new patch commits go via PR (fold-docker-patches); operator cuts tag v2.2.0-gorbagana.1 via the GitHub release UI post-merge (no local tags). Rebuild agent+deployer images from the tag. Nothing is deployed yet (staging included) — the new base is the first provenance pin for every environment. Spec §4.0/D1/D2/D8.

Observed 2026-06-10 during UI bridging tests on the local single-host deployment.

WARN in the relayer logs (hyperlane-core/src/rpc_clients/fallback.rs:246), emitted from lander's finality stage while confirming a delivery tx the relayer had just submitted to gorchain:

  WARN hyperlane_core::rpc_clients::fallback: Got error from inner fallback provider,
  error: Other(ClientError(Error { request: Some(GetTransaction), kind: SerdeJson(
  Error("invalid type: null, expected struct EncodedConfirmedTransactionWithStatusMeta", line: 0, column: 0)) }))
  provider: RpcClient { url: http://gorchain-rpc:8899/ }
  in lander finality_stage try_process_tx; tx status: Included, submission_attempts: 1, domain: gorchain

What we know:
- The RPC returned null for getTransaction on the just-submitted tx hash; the client cannot deserialize null into EncodedConfirmedTransactionWithStatusMeta, the fallback provider logs the WARN, and the stage retries.
- A solana->gorchain USDC transfer via the warp UI delivered successfully end-to-end while this WARN appeared, so it did not block that delivery.

Not yet verified:
- Whether the WARN is transient (tx not yet queryable at the polled commitment on the single-node chain, retries converge) or persistent (same hash recurring indefinitely).
- Whether the gorchain node's RPC serves transaction history (if disabled, getTransaction returns null permanently and finality can never confirm).

To investigate:
- Count recurrence of a single tx hash over time in relayer logs (kubectl -n laconic-hyperlane-relayer logs ... | grep -c <hash>).
- Check the gorchain node's RPC flags (transaction history / full RPC API) in the chain setup.
- If persistent, the fix is on the gorchain node config, not the relayer.
payload.title: Relayer finality stage WARNs: getTransaction returns null on gorchain (serde error)

payload.description: deployment/spec-warp-ui.yml serves host-name bridge.gorbagana.wtf (the dns_zone apex), but ops/roles/dns_cloudflare reconciles only the dns_records names (warp-ui -> warp-ui.bridge.gorbagana.wtf) — no A record for the apex is ever created, so stack_deploy preflight (hostname-resolution check) will fail on a prod deploy unless the apex record exists out-of-band. Staging avoided this by serving warp-ui.staging.gorbagana.wtf (see 2026-06-10-staging-ops-design.md). Fix direction: either add an apex entry mechanism to dns_records (relative '@'-style handling in ops/roles/dns_cloudflare/tasks/main.yml) or move prod warp-ui to warp-ui.bridge.gorbagana.wtf — operator decision, the apex is the published UI URL.

payload.description: The ops-lint workflow runs 'ansible-lint .' from ops/ which only processes 2 files (likely a discovery quirk with the explicit '.' argument), whereas argument-less 'ansible-lint' autodiscovers 83 files and currently finds 1 pre-existing production-profile failure: no-handler at ops/playbooks/local-access.yml:55 ('Refresh the CA bundle' task with when:changed, introduced in PR #34). Implement operator-attended bridge maintenance ops playbooks (Privy-signed)

payload.description:
The ops layer (PRs #25/#30) implemented bring-up (deploy-all.yml, setup-all.yml, prepare-chains, distribute-credentials, configure-dns, publish-bridge-state, stop-all) but NONE of the operator-attended maintenance playbooks the design calls for. docs/ops-decisions.md specifies seven composite playbooks; ops/playbooks/ contains none of them:

  kill-switch.yml      MISSING
  restore.yml          MISSING
  ism-update.yml       MISSING
  teardown.yml         MISSING
  add-validator.yml    MISSING
  remove-validator.yml MISSING
  verify-ownership.yml MISSING

Trigger: ops can now deploy N validators off validators.yaml (deploy-all.yml Validators play) — pod + MinIO IAM + DNS — but nothing updates the on-chain multisig ISM validator set. A newly-deployed validator announces to validator-announce and writes checkpoints to MinIO, but its H160 is not in any ISM, so the relayer's ISM verification ignores its signatures. The deployment side and the on-chain side were designed as separate operator actions (docs/architecture-decisions.md); only the deployment side shipped.

SIGNING MODEL CHANGED (2026-06-11): the bridge owner is now a Privy Solana server wallet (BRIDGE_OWNER_PUBKEY), NOT a Ledger hardware wallet — see docs/ops-decisions.md top section. On-chain steps must sign with the Privy bridge-owner wallet via the Privy API (operator-attended, run on the controller). The previous plan's built-in-Ledger signing path (forked sealevel-client --keypair usb://ledger...) is dropped; the fork keeps the Ledger code but it is unused. The signing mechanics (how a controller-run client signs through Privy — e.g. a Privy remote-signer mode in the forked client, or building+signing the tx via the Privy RPC endpoints) need a design pass before implementation.

The old BLOCKED ON (Ledger-support PR validation) no longer applies.

Reference: the archived single-validator k8s-Job pattern in deployment/ops-archive/scripts/restore.sh + templates/restore-job.yml.j2 shows the old set-validators-and-threshold call shape (pre-ansible). The 2026-05-29 ops-layer redesign spec is authoritative for the operator-layer structure but superseded on the signing backend. Builds on the ISM-ownership-handoff work in hyp-d9c (the bridge owner owns the ISM, so it can authorize set-validators-and-threshold).

payload.title: ism-update.yml — set ISM (validators, threshold) per chain, Privy-signed

The forked hyperlane-sealevel-client validates the synthetic token's metadataUri on NON-testnet chains and panics if it is missing or its contents mismatch (rust/sealevel/client/src/warp_route.rs ~:455-500: fetches the URI, parses SplTokenOffchainMetadata, asserts name/symbol equal the route config; testnet chains skip validation). The prod warp menu already carries the placeholder: deployment/bridges/default/warp-routes/usdc.yml metadataUri: REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN_METADATA_URI.

Before the prod warp deploy: (1) author the offchain metadata JSON for the gorchain synthetic USDC (fields: name, symbol, description?, image/logo — name/symbol MUST match the route menu's remote.name/remote.symbol), (2) decide hosting (must be a stable public HTTPS URL — e.g. raw.githubusercontent on the org, or the gorbagana site), (3) fill metadataUri in the prod menu. The warp deploy then embeds it via spl-token initialize-metadata (Token-2022 metadata extension) so wallets render the synthetic with name/symbol/logo. Staging/local deliberately leave metadataUri empty (testnet path skips validation; name/symbol still embedded).
payload.title: Prod warp deploy requires a hosted token-metadata JSON (metadataUri)

payload.description:
The forked hyperlane-sealevel-client validates the synthetic token's metadataUri on NON-testnet chains and panics if it is missing or its contents mismatch (rust/sealevel/client/src/warp_route.rs ~:455-500: fetches the URI, parses SplTokenOffchainMetadata {name, symbol, description (required), image (required, must return 200), website?, attributes?}; asserts name/symbol equal the route config; testnet chains skip validation when the uri is empty). The prod warp menu carries the placeholder: deployment/bridges/default/warp-routes/usdc.yml metadataUri: REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN_METADATA_URI.

STAGING NOW HAS THE TEMPLATE (2026-06-11): deployment/staging/bridges/default/warp-routes/usdc.yml carries REPLACE_WITH_STAGING_USDC_METADATA_URI, the staging runbook's 'One-time env fact' prerequisite shows the exact JSON (gist-hostable; image points at the canonical solana-labs token-list USDC logo, verified 200), and load_warp_routes' sanity gate refuses any REPLACE_WITH surviving in a selected route file.

Before the prod warp deploy: (1) author the prod metadata JSON (name/symbol MUST match the prod menu's remote.name/remote.symbol), (2) decide hosting — prefer something more durable than a gist for prod (e.g. a public gorbagana-dev repo raw URL or the gorbagana site), (3) fill metadataUri in the prod menu. The deploy embeds it via spl-token initialize-metadata (Token-2022 metadata extension).

load_validators.yml defaults to <repo>/{deployment_subdir}/bridges/{bridge_name}/operator/validators.yaml; prod deployment_subdir=deployment but deployment/bridges/default/ has only warp-routes/ — no operator/validators.yaml (staging+local both ship one). deploy-all.yml and restart-stack.yml include load_validators unconditionally, so a prod run dies at "Read validators.yaml" with a raw file lookup error instead of a legible assert. Also: ops/scripts/check-spec-parity.py:19-20 globs only spec-*.yml so bridges/** asymmetry passes CI, and there is no ops/tests/test_prod_env.yml to catch prod-only drift (local+staging have env tests). Fix: commit the prod validators.yaml pair (labels gorchain-primary/solana-primary, real hosts/hostnames), extend the parity gate to bridges/** file sets, add test_prod_env.yml mirroring test_staging_env.yml.

payload.description: deployment/staging/spec-monitoring.yml:25-26 (and prod/local siblings) carry MONITORED_WALLETS_*: "relayer:ADDR:5.0,igp-oracle:ADDR:2.0". ADDR matches neither REPLACE_WITH[A-Z0-9_]* nor __[A-Z0-9_]+__ so the render_spec.yml:125-134 placeholder gate passes it and monitoring deploys watching the literal string ADDR — wallet-balance alerting is silently dead on every env. Fix direction: rename the sentinel to REPLACE_WITH_RELAYER_ADDR / REPLACE_WITH_ORACLE_ADDR so the gate catches it, and render real addresses (relayer signer + igp oracle pubkey are both known to ops: addresses.env + igp_oracle_pubkey) via spec_token_renders.

payload.description: Observed on the first staging deploy: /srv/kind/hyperlane/bridge/logs/svm-deployer-*.log contains "Running command: ... --url https://devnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=<full key> ..." for every solana program deploy. Two layers: (1) the fork prints every spawned command verbatim — hyperlane-monorepo rust/sealevel/client/src/cmd_utils.rs:230 and warp_route.rs:440 println!("Running command: {:?}"); (2) the stacks deploy scripts tee all stdout unredacted — stack_orchestrator/data/config/deployer-scripts-config/deploy.sh:28 exec > >(tee -a $LOG_FILE) 2>&1 (warp-deployer script same pattern). Scope: NOT published (publish-bridge-state stages generated/ only and secret-scans; hyp-d34.1 closed that vector) but the key sits in plaintext on the host and in kubectl logs. Fix direction, both layers: (a) stacks defense-in-depth now — insert a redaction stage in the exec pipeline of both deploy.sh files, e.g. exec > >(stdbuf -o0 sed -E "s/api-key=[A-Za-z0-9-]+/api-key=REDACTED/g" | tee -a $LOG_FILE) 2>&1, which scrubs the log file AND pod stdout; (b) fork — redact query-string credentials in the command echo at the two println sites (rides the next vX.Y.Z-gorbagana.N release).
payload.title: Helius api-key printed in deployer logs (fork CLI command echo, unredacted tee)

payload.description: Observed on staging+local: the (now-fixed-at-cause) timeout toast rendered "Transaction timed out, Unknown may be busy" — getChainDisplayName (src/features/chains/utils.ts in the warp-ui fork) returns Unknown only when multiProvider.tryGetChainMetadata(origin) is null in useTokenTransfer.ts:268 catch path; with our registry metadata it should fall back to toTitleCase(name)="Gorchain". So the multiProvider lacked the chain at toast time — possibly an interaction with the runtime multi-route config store (PR #31) rebuilding chains, or a stale fork build. Cosmetic (the underlying timeout was the missing WS route, fixed in hyperlane-stacks 3f8aea6), but the same lookup failure would mislabel any future origin-chain error toast. Repro: trigger any transfer error toast on gorchain origin and check the name.
payload.title: warp-ui timeout toast says Unknown instead of the origin chain name

payload.description: hyperlane-monorepo typescript/sdk/src/token/adapters/SealevelTokenAdapter.ts:670-677 getMedianPriorityFee returns 0 for any chainName != "solanamainnet"; our chains are named "solana"/"gorchain", so every warp transfer (UI-built populateTransferRemoteTx :493-517) carries setComputeUnitPrice(0). On congested devnet this already produced >60-90s inclusion -> the UI declared TransactionExpiredBlockheightExceededError ("Failed" tag + timeout toast) while the tx landed late (staging walkthrough 2026-06-12, screenshots in debug-logs/). On PROD this means 0-fee txs into the mainnet fee market — same broken UX with real funds, worse odds. Compounding: the tx is built on a finalized (~32-slot-stale) blockhash and partialSigned by the unique-message keypair so the wallet cannot refresh it. Fix direction: relax the gate to run getMedianPriorityFee (getRecentPrioritizationFees median, Helius supports it) for our solana chain at least; consider a floor constant. Lands in the monorepo fork TS packages; how the warp-ui consumes it determines the delivery (npm pin vs fork build — see hyp pebble on consumption if filed, else check hyperlane-warp-ui-template package.json).
payload.title: Warp transfers send zero priority fee on our SVM chains (SDK gates on chainName solanamainnet)

payload.description: The warp-ui runtime chain config hands the full SOLANA_RPC_URL to the browser: the spec injects it via secrets: envFrom (compose deliberately omits it, stack_orchestrator/data/compose/docker-compose-hyperlane-warp-ui.yml) and entrypoint renders it into the chains config the frontend fetches. We classify SOLANA_RPC_URL as a secret everywhere else (CLAUDE.md, publish secret-scan, hyp-d34.1, hyp-534), yet any visitor to staging.gorbagana.wtf can lift the devnet key from devtools — and prod would expose the PAID mainnet key (quota burn + plan abuse). Fix direction: browser-side solana RPC should be a public/anon endpoint — staging: https://api.devnet.solana.com (also gives the browser the public wss for tx confirmation); prod: decide between a public mainnet RPC (rate-limited), a key-less proxy we host, or a separate browser-scoped restricted key (Helius supports domain-allowlisted keys — likely best). Agents keep the secret Helius URL; only the warp-ui chain config changes.
payload.title: warp-ui ships the Helius RPC URL (embedded api-key) to every browser

payload.description: hyperlane-monorepo typescript/widgets/src/walletIntegrations/solana.ts:133-151 onSendTx confirm() relies on web3.js confirmTransaction blockheight strategy: success arrives ONLY via signatureSubscribe (one-shot WS notification); expiry is polled via getBlockHeight. A notification missed at the boundary (WS reconnect, late subscribe, slow inclusion) is missed forever -> TransactionExpiredBlockheightExceededError -> UI marks the transfer Failed even when the tx landed (observed on staging 2026-06-12; balance watcher then contradicts with a success toast). Fix: catch TransactionExpiredBlockheightExceededError and check connection.getSignatureStatuses([signature]) once (searchTransactionHistory: true) — if confirmed/finalized, treat as success and proceed to getTransaction. Small, self-contained, kills the false-Failed class for ANY slow-inclusion cause; complements (does not replace) the priority-fee fix.
payload.title: widgets confirm(): poll getSignatureStatuses before declaring blockheight-exceeded failure

payload.description: hyperlane-monorepo typescript/sdk SealevelTokenAdapter getMedianPriorityFee returns 0 for any chainName != "solanamainnet"; our chains are named "solana"/"gorchain", so every UI-built warp transfer carried setComputeUnitPrice(0). On congested devnet this produced >60-90s inclusion -> TransactionExpiredBlockheightExceededError ("Failed" tag + timeout toast) while the tx landed late (staging 2026-06-12). On PROD this means 0-fee txs into the mainnet fee market. UPSTREAM STATUS (checked 2026-06-12 vs hyperlane-monorepo main): NOT fixed — the solanamainnet gate is unchanged on main; we are not upstreaming. DELIVERY: pnpm patch on @hyperlane-xyz/sdk@25.5.0 in the warp-ui fork (patches/@hyperlane-xyz__sdk@25.5.0.patch, commit 103c4aab on the fork) — allowlists chain name "solana" alongside solanamainnet; fee derivation unchanged (padded median, floor 100k microlamports ~0.0001 SOL at 1M CU). gorchain stays 0-fee deliberately (instant inclusion). Verify on staging after the next warp-ui image publish; close when a forward transfer confirms cleanly under load.

widgets walletIntegrations/solana.ts confirm() relied on web3.js confirmTransaction blockheight strategy: success ONLY via signatureSubscribe (one-shot WS notification) — a notification missed at the boundary is missed forever -> landed transfers shown as Failed (staging 2026-06-12). UPSTREAM STATUS (checked 2026-06-12): FIXED upstream in hyperlane-monorepo fcb087da25 (#8592) — confirmation switched to HTTP getSignatureStatuses polling — first released in @hyperlane-xyz/widgets 31.2.0; upstream warp-ui template main pins 35.0.1, but our fork base (Warp UI v2) pins 25.5.0 and there is no newer stable template release as of today, so no rebase/bump (6+ majors of breaking API). DELIVERY: backported as a pnpm patch on @hyperlane-xyz/widgets@25.5.0 in the warp-ui fork (patches/@hyperlane-xyz__widgets@25.5.0.patch, commit 103c4aab) — drop the patch when we ever upgrade to widgets >= 31.2.0. Production build verified, both changes present in the emitted bundle. Close after a clean forward transfer on staging.

The warp-ui runtime chain config handed the full SOLANA_RPC_URL to the browser: entrypoint rendered it into public/chains.yaml, so any visitor could lift the key (curl https://<warp-ui>/chains.yaml — no devtools needed). Prod would expose the PAID mainnet key.

FIX (implemented, pending release + staging verify): same-origin RPC proxy in the warp-ui fork — /api/rpc/solana (src/features/rpcProxy/solanaRpcProxy.ts, fork branch solana-rpc-proxy) forwards an allowlisted JSON-RPC method set to the server-side SOLANA_RPC_URL; rejected methods return -32601 and log in the pod. Stacks side (branch warp-ui-rpc-proxy): entrypoint.sh renders solana rpcUrl as ${WARP_UI_PUBLIC_URL}/api/rpc/solana when WARP_UI_PUBLIC_URL is set; staging spec = https://staging.gorbagana.wtf, prod spec = https://bridge.gorbagana.wtf. Unset (e2e/local keyless RPCs) keeps the direct URL. Verified: 8 unit tests, pnpm build, live next-start smoke (getHealth forwarded, requestAirdrop rejected, GET 405); hostname-based active-chain detection (findChainByRpcUrl) stays unique since the UI domain appears only in solana's rpcUrl.

Residual (accepted): the proxy is an unauthenticated same-origin endpoint that spends Helius quota; containment = method allowlist + Helius-side rate limits. RECOMMENDED for prod: separate Helius key for the warp-ui (distinct from agents' key) so abuse is bounded to a cheap-to-rotate key.

Close after: fork release including solana-rpc-proxy is built+deployed, then verify on staging that /chains.yaml shows the proxy URL (no api-key) and a transfer round-trips through /api/rpc/solana.

payload.body: Staging walkthrough follow-up (2026-06-12): after the widgets HTTP-polling patch, forward transfers no longer show false Failed, but Backpack itself hung at 'Confirming Transaction' (UI stuck at SigningTransfer — wallet promise unresolved) while the transfer landed and the recipient-balance toast fired. Root cause is wallet-internal: Backpack blocks its dapp response on its own WS signatureSubscribe confirmation against the WALLET's configured RPC; the public devnet preset drops the notification. Verified by discriminating test: pointing Backpack's devnet RPC at Helius resolves it in seconds. Not fixable app-side; documented in ops/runbooks/staging.md §5 and specs/stack-specifications.md (Stack 8 known limitation). Mainnet defaults are reliable, so prod exposure is low.

payload.description:
On a fresh host, e2e (and any kind-based deploy via SO --perform-cluster-management) fails when SO loads images: 'kind load docker-image' errors with 'ctr ... images import --all-platforms ... content digest <sha> not found'.

Root cause: Docker 28+/29 enables the containerd image store (docker info shows io.containerd.snapshotter.v1). 'docker save' of a multi-arch Docker Hub image (minio/minio, prom/prometheus, grafana/grafana, python:3.12-alpine) exports the full multi-platform index but only host-platform content; kind's 'ctr import --all-platforms' then fails on a missing foreign-platform manifest digest. Single-arch ghcr.io/gorbagana-dev/* images load fine. Confirmed kind v0.24.0 does NOT fix it (still uses --all-platforms). Versions seen: kind v0.23.0/v0.24.0, Docker 29.3.0.

Confirmed workaround: disable the containerd image store on the host -- /etc/docker/daemon.json: {"features": {"containerd-snapshotter": false}}, restart docker, re-pull images. docker save then returns to the legacy single-manifest format and kind load works at any kind version.

Deferred fix direction (workaround exists; do not block):
1. Document the daemon.json requirement in tests/e2e/README.md Prerequisites.
2. Set features.containerd-snapshotter: false in the ops Docker install (ops/roles/prerequisites_privileged) so fresh prod/local-single-host bootstraps work too. Current kind pin: v0.23.0 in ops/roles/prerequisites_privileged/defaults/main.yml.
3. stack-orchestrator load_images_into_kind (helpers.py ~line 618) swallows kind's stderr -- _run_command uses subprocess.run(shell=True) without capture, so DeployerException prints a bare CompletedProcess with no output (cost a debugging round-trip). Capture and include kind stdout/stderr in the exception.

Status: deferred, unlikely to be actioned (low priority).
payload.title: e2e/bootstrap: kind image-load fails on fresh hosts with Docker containerd image store

payload.body: Layer (a) (stacks defense-in-depth) done: warp-deployer deploy.sh top-level log now redacts api-key= (matches the core deployer deploy.sh:28, which was already fixed). Both deployer scripts' exec pipelines scrub 'api-key=<key>' from the on-host log files AND pod stdout, so the fork's verbatim command echo is redacted before it lands anywhere — the host-plaintext + kubectl-logs exposure is closed. Per-route published log (deploy.sh:113) already redacts the whole SOLANA_RPC_URL and is left as-is (it must drop the literal 'api-key=' to pass publish-bridge-state's secret-scan). Remaining: layer (b) — redact query-string creds at the fork command-echo sites (cmd_utils.rs:230, warp_route.rs:440), source-side hardening that rides the next vX.Y.Z-gorbagana.N release. Keeping open until that lands.

Closing: the host-plaintext + kubectl-logs exposure is fully mitigated by the stacks redaction (both deployer scripts scrub api-key= from log files and pod stdout). Layer (b) — the fork command-echo redaction (cmd_utils.rs:230, warp_route.rs:440) — is unplanned; the wrapper-script redaction covers our deployment path, so the source-side change is not scheduled.

payload.description:
The hyperlane-explorer scraper is built from the gorbagana monorepo fork at v2.2.0-gorbagana.1 (agents v2.2.0), but the bridge's on-chain Hyperlane programs were deployed from 16c056a. The Sealevel scraper decodes mailbox/dispatch/delivery/gas-payment account layouts directly; if those layouts changed between 16c056a and v2.2.0, the scraper will mis-parse or skip messages and the explorer will show no/incorrect data.

Self-flagged in stack_orchestrator/data/stacks/hyperlane-explorer/stack.yml:6-9.

Action: deploy the explorer in local/staging, send a bridge transfer, and confirm a corresponding row lands in message_view (via the frontend /api/graphql). If layouts are incompatible, either repin the scraper's monorepo build to 16c056a or confirm the v2.2.0 sealevel indexer is backward-compatible.

Related: the e2e suite currently has no end-to-end 'message appears in explorer' assertion (test_15_explorer.py only smoke-checks pods/serving/domain query), so this can't be caught automatically yet.
